item.title: #3594796: Add a settings form and a requirements check for the content review judge
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594796 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

The content review judge in ai_eval_content_review now has a settings form at /admin/config/ai/ai-eval/content-review for the review rule, criterion, content type, body field and text format. It offers only choices that exist on the site. Previously these could only be changed with drush cset or config import, and a content type without the expected body field (as on a Drupal CMS page) made the criterion see only the title and score the answer 0 with no warning. Now a judge with settings that do not fit the site reports the answer as not measured, and the status report says what is wrong. New installs leave the content type, body field and text format unset, so a site owner must choose them before the judge can run. Existing sites keep their current values.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: New installs ship ai_eval_content_review.settings with bundle, body_field and body_format empty (previously page, body, basic_html); existing sites keep their values.
  • Permission change: New route /admin/config/ai/ai-eval/content-review is gated by the existing administer ai eval permission.
  • New API: New JudgeSettingsChecker service (ai_eval_content_review.settings_checker) with problems() and errors(); CriterionRunner takes it as a fifth constructor argument.

Technical details

A single JudgeSettingsChecker is shared by the form, the status report and the judge. problems() returns errors and warnings keyed by setting. Errors cover a missing rule, a missing criterion index, a missing or nonexistent content type, a body field that is unset, absent or not of type text, text_long or text_with_summary, an unset, nonexistent or disabled text format, a format the field's allowed_formats excludes, and extra_fields the type lacks. A warning is raised for a disabled rule, or for a rule that does not apply to the configured bundle. errors() returns only the blocking messages.

CriterionRunner::review() calls errors() before building the unsaved node. If any are returned it throws a RuntimeException ("The content review judge settings do not fit this site: ..."), so the judge records no measurement instead of reviewing a page without the answer. JudgeSettingsRequirements (hook_runtime_requirements) adds a status report row: "Not set up" (warning) when no rule is set, "Settings fit this site" (OK), "Check the settings" (warning) or "Cannot review" (error). JudgeSettingsForm is a ConfigFormBase that filters the criterion, body field and format selects by the chosen rule, content type and field, and redraws them with htmx. It warns when the criterion changes, since existing judges then check another criterion and need validating again. Earlier validations are not marked stale. The default config/install values for bundle, body_field and body_format are now empty strings.

Upgrade

Custom code that constructs CriterionRunner directly must pass the new ai_eval_content_review.settings_checker service (JudgeSettingsChecker) as the fifth argument. On new installs, open /admin/config/ai/ai-eval/content-review and choose the content type, body field and text format before running the judge.

item.title: #3594795: Judge content review criteria without saving a node
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594795 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

The AI Eval content review judge no longer saves and deletes a temporary unpublished node for every judged answer. The page is built in memory and reviewed without being saved, so automators, search indexing and other save hooks stop running per answer. That removes the extra LLM call per judged answer and the search index warning for the deleted node. Records made by the judge are visible only to users with "configure reviews" and are hidden from the AI Content Review review queue. A criterion that needs a saved entity cannot be judged this way.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Requirements: ai_eval_content_review now depends on the entity module.
  • Database update: ai_eval_content_review_update_10001() installs the ai_eval_page review record bundle with an eval_key field.
  • Permission change: Records of type ai_eval_page and their suggestions require "configure reviews" to view, and are hidden from the AI Content Review review queue.
  • API change: CriterionRunner constructor takes a new fourth argument, the ai_eval_content_review.eval_pages service (EvalPageRegistry).

Technical details

AI Content Review's internal record type reloads the reviewed entity by id, so it cannot review an unsaved one. The submodule now ships its own review_record bundle plugin, ai_eval_page, with an eval_key bundle field. CriterionRunner::review() builds the node with create() and does not save it. It wraps the node and a random key in a new EvalPage value object, which is deliberately not an entity because the internal record type claims every entity. The EvalPage is registered in a request-scoped EvalPageRegistry (service ai_eval_content_review.eval_pages) and passed to the real ReviewOrchestrator::runCriterion(). The record type looks the page up by key. It gives the criterion the same review context lines as for a saved node, with the node as its node token context, and it applies no rules and refuses suggestions. In a finally block, deleteReviews() removes the records and their suggestions by eval_key, and the page is removed from the registry.

Access: AI Content Review alpha3 checks the reviewed subject only for records about a Drupal entity, so ai_eval_page records and their suggestions would be viewable with "view review records". EvalPageAccess forbids view, update and delete of them, and of their suggestions, without "configure reviews". Two pages in AI Content Review do not check entity access. A route subscriber adds JudgedPageRecordAccessCheck to the record detail route (/ai-content-review/record/{record_id}/detail), and a form alter on the review queue removes ai_eval_page rows for everyone and leaves them out of the waiting count.

Limit: the criterion gets an entity with no id. Tools that reload the node by id (for example GetCurrentContentEntityValues) and resumed runs cannot see it. The extra_fields setting still fills extra values on the unsaved node, but automators no longer fill them.

Upgrade

Run database updates. ai_eval_content_review_update_10001() installs the ai_eval_page review record bundle on existing sites. The submodule now also depends on the entity module, which AI Content Review already requires. Code that constructs CriterionRunner directly must pass the new fourth argument, the ai_eval_content_review.eval_pages service:

ai_eval_content_review.eval_pages:
  class: Drupal\ai_eval_content_review\EvalPageRegistry

item.title: #3594794: Add a judge for every criterion of a review rule
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594794 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

The AI Eval content review judge now covers every criterion of every AI Content Review rule, not just the one at the site-wide criterion_index. A rule with three criteria such as Tone & voice, Inclusive language and Grammar now has three judges. Existing judges keep their ids, so their scores and validations stay attached to the same criterion. The drush scoring command can target one criterion, and importing a fixture refuses to continue when the criterion at its recorded position has since changed label.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: Optional trailing criterion position argument on CriterionRunner::reviewAsJudge(), judgeModel(), editorsModel(), review(), criterion() and ReviewRuleJudges::judgeId(); new content_review_criterion_at__<rule>__<index> judge ids; new --criterion drush option on ai-eval-cr:score-items.

Technical details

ReviewRuleJudges::graderInfoAlter() now loops over every criterion of each review_rule, plus the criterion_index from settings even if the rule has no criterion there. The criterion at that position keeps the existing id (content_review_criterion, or content_review_criterion__<rule> for other rules). All other positions get content_review_criterion_at__<rule>__<index>, counting from 0. This prefix is disjoint from the older ids, so a rule id containing criterion_1 or __ cannot collide with an existing judge. If another module already declares an id, that judge is skipped and a warning is logged. Ids follow positions, as AI Content Review's own {rule}__{index} names do, so reordering a rule's criteria moves its judges. Judge definitions carry criterion_index and criterion_label, and the label reads "Content review: <rule> / <criterion>".

CriterionRunner::reviewAsJudge(), judgeModel(), editorsModel(), review() and criterion(), and ReviewRuleJudges::judgeId(), take an optional trailing criterion position (judgeId() also takes the default index). drush ai-eval-cr:score-items has a new --criterion option (a position from 0, defaulting to the settings value) and writes criterion_index and criterion_label into the fixture meta. import-run rebuilds the judge id from that meta and errors with a request to give --grader when the label now at that position differs from the recorded one. The CHANGELOG notes it cannot distinguish criteria that share a label.

Upgrade

Callers of the listed CriterionRunner methods and ReviewRuleJudges::judgeId() need no change: the new criterion position argument is optional and trailing. To score a non-default criterion from drush:

drush ai-eval-cr:score-items --items=items.yaml --criterion=2 --out=/tmp/out.yaml

Fixtures scored before this change have no criterion_index and import against the judge for the criterion_index in settings.

item.title: #3594790: Show how many questions were measured next to the pass rate
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594790 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

When some questions error out or can't be scored, the pass rate is calculated only over the questions that were measured. The drush run summary and the result detail page now say so next to the pass rate, for example "9 of 12 measured", so a "100%" is no longer easy to read as 100% of all 12 questions. The text appears only when fewer than all questions were measured.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

In EvalRunCommand, the target result line now carries the count inside the parentheses after the pass rate, such as (pass_rate: 100% [70.1%–100%], 9 of 12 measured: 3 errors) [PASS] 34s. The reasons for missing questions (N errors, N unscored) are listed after the count. This replaces the old trailing (3 errors) / (3 unscored) suffix after the duration. The measured count uses valid_count from the result, falling back to total questions minus errors minus unscored. The same value is reused by the existing insufficient-coverage warning.

In EvalResultsController, the pass-rate cell on the result detail page computes $measuredCount once (question_count - error_count - unscored) and uses it for the existing (passed / total) figure. It appends , N of M measured when $measuredCount is below question_count.

item.title: #3594788: Validate a judge only on answers it scored
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594788 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

Validating a judge that has no dimension (decision rubric, content review) in the browser used to read every pass or fail given on any results page, whatever the judge. A review now counts for a judge only when that judge scored that answer in that result: a score was recorded without an error, and a zero counts. Reviews from another test, or on answers the judge failed to score, are left out. The validation report and the calibration page now say that reviews are whole-answer verdicts while a judge may check only some rules. Per-judge verdicts are a follow-up (#3594789).

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: HumanLabelSourceInterface gains unattributedAnnotationCount(); any class implementing the interface must add it.
  • New API: HumanLabelSourceInterface::unattributedAnnotationCount() returns how many results-page reviews cannot be attributed to any judge.

Technical details

HumanLabelSource::forGrader() previously ignored $graderId. It now passes it to fromAnnotations(), which calls hydrateFromResult() and keeps an annotation only if the grader id appears among the entries in that question's grader_scores in the stored ai_eval_result.scores_json with a numeric score and no error. Errored entries and entries with a NULL score (not applicable) do not count. Annotations are still merged only on the holistic path, when both $domainTags and $dimension are NULL. Review labels from ai_eval_review_label (dimension-scoped) are unchanged.

A result stored without grader_scores cannot say which judges scored it, so its annotations count for no judge. The new unattributedAnnotationCount() counts those, one per (result, question), and the validation page shows the number for judges without a dimension. The docs entry JUDGE-L13 in docs/semantic/tech/JUDGE_01_JudgeValidation.md was updated to match.

Upgrade

Reviews on results stored before AI Eval recorded which judges scored each answer no longer count for any judge's validation. They are kept, not deleted, and the judge's validation page says how many were left out. Run the test again and review the new results.

Custom classes implementing HumanLabelSourceInterface must add:

public function unattributedAnnotationCount(): int;

item.title: #3586640: [Meta] ai_disclosure: EU AI Act Article 50 transparency module
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal plan
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586640 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

This is the meta plan for a new standalone module, ai_disclosure, which helps sites meet Article 50 of the EU AI Act (applicable since 2 August 2026). It lets editors record how AI was involved in each piece of content, works out whether a visible label is legally required, and shows readers an EU-icon disclosure. It also outputs machine-readable markers and adds a compliance report at /admin/reports/ai-disclosure. At the time of the last update, the foundation, field, widget, formatter, marking, recorder API, report and multilingual child issues are checked off. The documentation issue and the companion integrations for other AI modules are still open.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: Planned public DisclosureRecorder API with suggest() and apply() methods, plus a DisclosureResolver service, in the new ai_disclosure module.

Technical details

The plan describes an ai_disclosure field type added per bundle, one disclosure per entity translation. Its modes are inherit (uses the bundle default and stores no data), none, profile and custom.

Grades are config entities with stable machine names: human_only, ai_metadata, ai_rated, ai_translated, ai_summarized, ai_partly_assisted, ai_assisted_hitl, ai_generated_autonomous and ai_deepfake. Each carries severity, EU icon mapping, a label-required flag, a review-exemptible flag, a disclosure sentence and an IPTC digitalSourceType URI. Disclosure profiles are also config entities. They hold a grade, a human-review flag, editorial responsibility and a shared markdown description that all inheriting content uses.

The DisclosureResolver service decides whether a label is required with grade.label_required && !(human_review && grade.review_exemptible). The human-review exemption applies to text only, so deep-fake grades cannot be exempted by review. The formatter renders the EU icon, the per-grade sentence and an expandable "How was AI used?" section. A site policy setting chooses between labelling only when required and always disclosing. JSON-LD and meta output carry the IPTC digitalSourceType.

The public DisclosureRecorder API is the integration surface. AI tools call suggest(), which shows the editor an Accept/Dismiss callout, or apply() for headless pipelines. The dependency direction is deliberately inverted, so ai_disclosure knows nothing about specific AI tools. Out of scope for 1.0: Art. 50(1) chatbot notices, C2PA or watermark file embedding, AI-content detection, and retroactive labelling of content published before 2026-08-02.

This summary comes from the issue body only. No code diff was attached, so the details above describe the plan, not reviewed code.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: August 3, 2026

  • afoster (Foster Interactive Inc.)

item.title: #3594782: --as-user and caller_uid do not switch the Drupal account
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594782 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

drush ai-eval:run --as-user=<uid> and a question's caller_uid now really run the agent or chat call as that Drupal user. Before, the uid only went to an optional ai_eval.caller_context service that AI Eval does not ship, so on most sites the agent ran as the current account, which is anonymous under drush. With AI Metering that meant eval runs spent the anonymous visitors' shared monthly token budget, and could exhaust it. 0 means anonymous on purpose, and a uid with no account fails that question with "caller uid N has no account" instead of silently running as someone else. Judges and graders are not switched.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

In EvalRunner::runQuestion() the caller uid (caller_uid, or the run's --as-user default) is turned into an account by a new private callerAccount(): uid 0 gives AnonymousUserSession, otherwise the user entity is loaded via entity_type.manager. If none loads, the question returns a failed result with error set to caller uid %d has no account without invoking anything. Otherwise account_switcher->switchTo() is called just before the chat or agent invocation, and switchBack() runs in a nested finally, after callerContext?->clear(), so the original account is restored even if the caller context throws. The caller context service is still told the uid as before. EvalRunner gets two new optional trailing constructor arguments, ?AccountSwitcherInterface and ?EntityTypeManagerInterface, wired in ai_eval.services.yml as @account_switcher and @entity_type.manager. When no switcher is injected, no switching happens. The --as-user option help and the running.md warning were rewritten, and a kernel test CallerAccountSwitchTest was added.

Upgrade

Agent tests run from drush without --as-user or caller_uid still run as anonymous. The updated docs recommend running them as a dedicated eval user, for example drush ai-eval:run --target=<agent test> --as-user=<uid>. Check that any existing caller_uid values point to real users, since a missing account now fails the question. Subclasses or custom service definitions that construct EvalRunner directly need no change, as the new constructor arguments are optional.

Contribution

item.title: #3594783: The run drops the agent's own error when it does not answer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594783 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

When an agent gives no answer during an AI Eval run, the run now keeps the reason. Previously each question showed only "invocation failed" and the log said "returned solvability 0". Now the agent's own error, such as an AI Metering "Monthly AI token quota exceeded" message, is included in the warning log and stored with the question result. The results detail page shows it under an "Error:" section.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

In EvalRunner, a new per-question property lastInvocationError is reset at the start of each question. When invokeAgent() gets no answer, it reads getLastError() from the agent wrapper if the method is callable (it can be empty) and appends it to the "not solvable" and "solved but returned empty" warnings. The same property is also filled from the catch blocks in invokeAgent() and the chat invocation, and for the missing-agent-id and agent-not-found cases. Text goes through the new capErrorDetail(), which collapses whitespace and cuts to 300 characters, because provider errors can echo parts of the request.

For a failed question, the result row gets an error_detail key next to error. error keeps its fixed value, so existing readers are unaffected, and error_detail is only present when something supplied a reason. EvalResultsController renders an "Error:" section in the question details, with error_detail appended after a colon. Tests in ToolCallCaptureTest cover both an agent-reported error and a thrown exception reaching the row, and ResultsDetailReadabilityTest covers the display.

item.title: #3594784: Let the decision rubric judge see the question as well as the answer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594784 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

The decision rubric judge can now see the test question as well as the answer. Previously it only received the answer, so rules such as "do not add facts that answer a different question" or "reply in the visitor's language" could not be judged. Set the new optional input_key in ai_eval.decision_rubric and every rule is asked with the question under that name. Left empty, nothing changes and stored calibrations keep applying. Once it is set, any calibration fitted on the answer alone stops applying and you need to fit a new one. The issue's demo-site validation (72 labeled answers) showed mixed results: fewer missed padding errors, but lower overall true positive rate. The author says the rule wording is probably the next thing to tune.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: New optional input_key in ai_eval.decision_rubric; empty (default) keeps current behavior and stored calibrations.

Technical details

DecisionRubric gains a readonly inputKey property, read from config input_key and trimmed, defaulting to an empty string. In DecisionRubricGrader::grade(), when inputKey is non-empty the Decision state becomes [$rubric->inputKey => $input, $rubric->stateKey => $response]. Otherwise it stays [$rubric->stateKey => $response]. DecisionRubric::fingerprint() adds input_key to the fingerprint settings only when it is set, so a rubric without it keeps its old fingerprint and its stored calibrations stay valid. A rubric with it gets a new fingerprint, since a curve fitted on the answer alone says nothing about judging with the question. problem() now refuses an input_key equal to state_key, because the answer would overwrite the input in the state array. The config schema ai_eval.decision_rubric has the new input_key string. docs/user/usage/calibration.md gains a paragraph that suggests wording the rubric's question to mention the visitor's question and the assistant's reply.

Upgrade

Optional. To let the judge see the question, set input_key in ai_eval.decision_rubric (the docs use question as an example) and reword the rubric question to say it is given a question and a reply. Then refit the calibration, because the fingerprint changes. Existing configs without input_key need no action.

Contribution

item.title: #3594781: Judges fail on models that refuse temperature; make the pin optional
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594781 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

LLM judges are pinned to temperature 0 and top_p 1 where the provider offers them. Some models, such as Claude Haiku 5.5, reject temperature, and every judged question then failed and the run measured nothing. Now, if a model refuses a pinned setting, the judge asks again without the pin and the run records the judge as not pinned. A new settings checkbox, "Pin judges to temperature 0" (on by default), lets a site turn pinning off entirely and use the provider defaults.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Database update: ai_eval_update_10048() sets pin_judge_decoding to TRUE on existing sites.
  • Config change: New pin_judge_decoding boolean in ai_eval.settings (default TRUE), with schema and a checkbox on the settings form.

Technical details

The setting is stored as pin_judge_decoding and read in LlmJudgeBase::create(). A public setPinDecoding() setter exists for tests. pinDeterministicDecoding() returns early when pinning is off or the model has already refused. It also keeps the provider configuration without the pinned knobs in unpinnedConfiguration.

The chat call moved into a new private askJudge(), used both directly and inside the rate-limit handler callback. On an exception, refusesPinnedKnob() checks whether the message names a knob that was actually pinned (temperature or top_p, with spellings such as top-p and topP) within a few words of a refusal term (deprecated, unsupported, not supported, invalid, and similar). A message that only echoes the request, such as an invalid API key with temperature=0 in it, does not match. On a match, the provider is reset to the unpinned configuration, lastPinnedDecoding is set to [] so the run identity records no pin, and the call is retried once. Any other error is rethrown as before, so a broken provider does not cost two calls per question. A retry that hits a rate limit goes through the existing rate-limit handler.

The refusal is remembered in a static $pinRefused array keyed by provider and model. It is static because stepped runs create a new judge per question. So the extra call happens once per process and model, not once per question.

Upgrade

Run drush updatedb to apply ai_eval_update_10048(), which sets pin_judge_decoding: true and keeps the existing behavior. To use provider defaults, uncheck "Pin judges to temperature 0" on the settings form, or set pin_judge_decoding: false in ai_eval.settings.

item.title: #3585933: Authorization denials surface as -32603 Internal server error, because the SDK dispatch loop swallows the exception
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 2.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3585933 · 1 contributor · 18 comments

Summary

Per-call authorization denials thrown from an SDK RequestEvent subscriber never produced a 401 or 403. The SDK's per-message guard turned them into an HTTP 200 with JSON-RPC -32603 Internal server error and an error-level log entry. The fix does not make that path work. It removes the handling that could never run and states the supported route: authorization belongs in a PSR-15 transport middleware, which answers a denial with its own 401 or 403 response before the SDK dispatches. Custom authorization code, and mcp_server_oauth 1.0.0-alpha1 (which still throws the exception), cannot deny calls this way. That code needs to move to middleware.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: McpServerController, McpExceptionSubscriber and the drush mcp:server command no longer catch or translate McpAuthorizationDeniedException; McpExceptionSubscriber drops its logger constructor argument.
  • Deprecation: Drupal\mcp_server\Exception\McpAuthorizationDeniedException is deprecated in mcp_server:2.0.0-beta6 and removed in 3.0.0.

Technical details

The exception is thrown inside Protocol::doProcessInput()'s catch (\Throwable) guard, so the controller catch and McpExceptionSubscriber could not be reached. Of the three options in the issue, the merged change picks neither out-of-band signalling nor an SDK change. It deletes the dead code and points to the existing mcp_server.transport_middleware tag, where a middleware returns its own PSR-7 response without entering SDK dispatch or the kernel exception path.

Removed: the McpAuthorizationDeniedException catch in McpServerController::handle(), the matching catch and JSON-RPC error writing in McpServerCommands, and the exception branch in McpExceptionSubscriber::onException(). That subscriber now only rewrites the route-level AccessDeniedHttpException (access mcp server) into -32001/-32002 with 401/403, and its @logger.channel.mcp_server argument was dropped from mcp_server.exception_subscriber in mcp_server.services.yml. The exception class stays, marked @deprecated, only because mcp_server_oauth 1.0.0-alpha1 still throws it.

The change adds a test fixture, StateArmedDenyingMiddleware in mcp_server_test, which denies tools/call with 401 or 403 when armed through State. It also adds TransportMiddlewareDenialTest, and the README authorization section and the .ai/kenkeep notes now describe the middleware route. The kenkeep note also records that on SDK releases with php-sdk#528 the throw would escape to core as a 500 rather than -32603, so throwing from a subscriber cannot deny a call either way.

Upgrade

Replace a RequestEvent subscriber that throws McpAuthorizationDeniedException with a PSR-15 middleware registered under the existing tag, which returns the denial itself:

services:
  mcp_server_test.middleware.denying:
    class: Drupal\mcp_server_test\Middleware\StateArmedDenyingMiddleware
    tags:
      - { name: mcp_server.transport_middleware, priority: 50 }

In process(), return a PSR-7 response with status 401 or 403, JSON-RPC error code -32001 or -32002, and a WWW-Authenticate header, instead of calling $handler->handle($request). The test fixture StateArmedDenyingMiddleware shows the full pattern.

Contribution

item.title: #3518120: Define tools with attributes on typed methods
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 1.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3518120 · 4 contributors · 25 comments
  • Followers: 5
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 4 contributors

Summary

The Tool API module can now turn a public method of an existing service into a tool by adding PHP attributes, with no plugin class. The method's parameters become the tool's inputs, its return value becomes the output, and the docblock supplies the descriptions. Access is never inferred. Each tool must declare a permission, an access method, or an entity operation on each entity parameter. Existing #[Tool] plugins can also declare a typed __invoke() and get the same inference, so they can be converted one definition at a time. This landed in the 1.0.x-dev release.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: ToolBase::doExecute() is no longer abstract: a #[Tool] plugin may declare a typed __invoke() instead. Other changes to existing behavior are listed in the MR.
  • New API: New attributes ToolMethod, ToolInput, ToolEntityInput, ToolOutput and ToolProperty in Drupal\tool\Attribute, plus Drupal\tool\Tool\Method\MethodTool as the plugin class for method tools.

Technical details

#[ToolMethod] goes on a public service method, or on the class of an invokable service, where it applies to __invoke(). It requires an explicit id, because agent, ECA and MCP configuration refer to tools by ID. operation defaults to ToolOperation::Write. Access options are permission (same syntax as #[Tool]) and access (a service method returning an AccessResultInterface). Every entity parameter must use #[ToolEntityInput(op: ...)], which is checked through the entity's access handler. A method with no declared check fails discovery. An entity operation only counts if it sits on a required, single entity parameter.

#[ToolInput] refines a parameter. #[ToolOutput] names or refines the output, and two or more declare several outputs. An array{...} shape in @return also declares several outputs. #[ToolProperty] marks the public properties or zero-argument methods of a plain PHP value object to publish. Outputs can narrow to a subset with members:.

Inference reads native and docblock types: scalars, entities, backed enums, DateTime, lists, and array{} shapes. Unsupported parameter types fail discovery.

Discovery runs in a compiler pass that scans service class sources for the attribute name before autoloading them. It records the results in the tool.method_tools container parameter, which the tool manager merges with plugin discovery. A definition that cannot be built is logged to the tool channel and skipped. The other tools still load. Definitions are cached, so a new attribute needs a cache rebuild.

A method may return an ExecutableResult to set its own message, failure category, or outputs on failure. Throwing Drupal\tool\Exception\InputException reports a caller error. Other exceptions are logged and the caller only learns that the run failed. For #[Tool] plugins, a typed __invoke() is used when doExecute() is not overridden, and a plugin that declares #[ToolEntityInput] parameters but overrides access() is skipped at discovery. The change also adds a docs page, docs/developers/tool-methods.md, and a Typed tools section in the creating-a-tool docs.

Upgrade

To convert an existing #[Tool] plugin, replace doExecute() and the input_definitions/output_definitions arrays with a typed __invoke():

#[ToolOutput(name: 'message')]
public function __invoke(string $name, ?string $greeting = NULL): string {
  return ($greeting ?? 'Hello') . ", $name!";
}

The required op on #[ToolEntityInput] adds an access check on every entity passed in, so a converted tool can deny calls the old plugin allowed. Throw InputException instead of \InvalidArgumentException for messages meant for the caller.

Summary

In AI Eval's admin forms, several fields that name something the site already knows no longer have to be typed from memory. A question's "Rubric reference" is a select of the site's enabled rubric versions. "Expected tools" suggest the AI module's function names and plugin ids. A question's domain bundle, its tags, a rubric's applicable bundles and a failure mode's taxonomy suggest values already in use on the site. The issue's other examples (test form "Proving-ground fixtures", calibration "Model") are not covered by the changes I found.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New ai_eval.reference_options service (ReferenceOptions) supplying rubric versions, tool names, bundles, dataset tags and failure mode taxonomies for form fields.

Technical details

The work lives in a new ReferenceOptions service (ai_eval.reference_options). forQuestionEditor() returns rubrics, tools, bundles and tags. bundles() combines the domain_bundle values of questions with the applicable_bundles in rubric data. datasetTags() reads tags from the questions of the current dataset. taxonomies() returns the taxonomy ids of existing failure modes plus default.

DatasetQuestionEditor::fields() takes an $options array. When rubrics is supplied, rubric_ref renders as a select with a (none) option. A stored ref the site does not have stays selected and is labelled "(not on this site)", so saving never silently drops it. Without options the old free-text fields remain. Suggestions for tools, bundles, tags and taxonomies are HTML <datalist> elements, so free text is still accepted. Each editor gets its own datalist id for its tool rows (TOOL_LIST_PREFIX), and the "+ Add" request carries it as a list query parameter so added rows use the same suggestions. FailureModeForm now injects ReferenceOptions and attaches a taxonomy datalist to its taxonomy_id field.

item.title: #3594774: Buttons and workflow steps that promise what they do not do
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594774 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

The AI Eval guided test and workflow page no longer promise things they did not do. "Save and run" on the Review step now saves the test and starts a run, then opens the workflow page, which shows the run's progress. Chat tests no longer offer the prompt optimizer, which only works on agent tests; the step now says so. The steps in tabs A and B open this test's own dataset, rubrics and judges (a dropbutton when there are several) instead of the site-wide lists. Step A1 no longer promises generated cases. Because "Save and run" now starts a run, it can incur provider charges, and the form says so.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: WorkflowStateService takes the dataset loader and rubric loader as optional fifth and sixth constructor arguments, GuidedTestForm takes the eval runner, and workflow step descriptors may carry action_links and requires_permissions.
  • New API: RubricLoader::loadEntity() is new, and step descriptors accept action_links (list of {label, route, params}) rendered as a dropbutton.

Technical details

GuidedTestForm::saveAndRun() now calls EvalRunnerInterface::startRun($target, 'ui') after the finalizer saves the draft. If the start throws, the save stands. When activeRunForTarget() returns a run, the form shows "A run is already in progress." as a warning. Any other failure is shown as "The run could not start: @reason". The button and a cost note are rendered only when $unresolved === [], so a selected judge with no model hides the run.

WorkflowStateService gets the dataset loader and rubric loader as optional constructor arguments. It uses them to build step descriptors with action_links (rubrics the test's questions name, LLM judges the test uses, the test's dataset). WorkflowRibbon::accessibleLinks() filters those by access. With more than one link it renders a dropbutton whose first item keeps the step's label. With exactly one accessible link, that link replaces the collection route. The test's own route is used only when no specific link is known, so the collection link remains the fallback. TargetDashboardController attaches core/drupal.dropbutton, since tab switches swap in fragments that carry no libraries. For chat-mode targets (mode === 'chat') the optimize step becomes not-started with the badge "Agent tests only" and no action. The re-run step text changes, and a leftover pending candidate no longer blocks it.

The same commit also added a requires_permissions descriptor key, used to note the Annotate permission next to the Annotate step's link (tracked in #3594776). It also scoped the error-analysis counts to the current test (#3594775).

Upgrade

Code that constructs these classes directly needs the new arguments. GuidedTestForm now requires ai_eval.eval_runner (and ai_eval.reference_options, from #3594777). WorkflowStateService accepts the dataset loader and rubric loader as optional fifth and sixth arguments, so existing constructions still work but the rubric step then links to the rubric list.

item.title: #3594769: Pass-rate wording: a range "above and below" 0% or 100%, and a last-run card that mixes scopes
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594769 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

The AI Eval small-sample advisory no longer says a pass rate's range "extends about X% above and below" the reported rate. That wording was wrong at 0% and 100% (it implied values past the edges) and for the Wilson interval, which is not symmetric. It now states the actual bounds, for example a range between 0% and 39%. The Results list card previously labelled "Last Eval Run" mixed two scopes. It is now labelled "Latest result per test", and the passing, test, question and duration figures all come from the same rows.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The change landed inside the combined Sprint 7 commit dcbcdf0 in the ai_eval repository. It was not a separate commit for this issue.

In src/Render/PowerAdvisory.php the @half argument is dropped. When per-question counts are available, the advisory calls wilsonInterval() on the sample size service at the configured confidence. Otherwise it uses the stored $ciLow and $ciHigh. The bounds are shown in whole percents, or with up to three decimals when needed so the displayed range is wider than the displayed margin of error. Counted verdicts produce "At N% confidence the true rate is likely between X and Y…". Without counts the text says "The run reports a likely range of X to Y…", since those bounds come from the producer. @confidence now reports supportedConfidence(), the level the arithmetic actually used.

In EvalResultsController, the question and duration totals are now summed over $targetHealth, the latest result per test. This is the same set that feeds the passing and test counts. The old loop summed any rows within 300 seconds of the newest result. The latest-results query adds orderBy('id', 'ASC') so that two results from the same second resolve to the newest row. The card label becomes "Latest result per test", and the counts use formatPlural() ("N tests", "N questions"). The stored pass-rate range in the results table also gets a tooltip saying it is stored at 95% confidence on this site. A functional test, ResultsLastRunCardTest, covers the card.

item.title: #3594778: Dataset Save drops an open question editor without a warning
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594778 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

On a dataset's edit page, pressing the dataset's Save while a question editor was open and unsaved used to discard the question with no warning. Now the dataset's Save is stopped and the editor shows "Save or cancel this question first. The dataset's Save does not save it." Closing or leaving the page with unsaved question edits also asks for confirmation. The question's own Save is still what stores the question.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The question editor is its own htmx form inside the dataset form, so the dataset form's Save never submitted it. The fix is client-side, in js/dataset-csrf.js. Any input event inside form.ai-eval-q-editor sets a data-ai-eval-unsaved attribute on the editor. A capture-phase click handler sets it too when a repeater row is added or removed (.ai-eval-rep-add, .ai-eval-rep-remove), because those fire no input event. An editor the server returns with .ai-eval-q-errors is also marked unsaved. The editor's own Save or Cancel swaps or removes it, which clears the mark.

While an editor is marked, a capture-phase submit listener cancels submission of any other form (the dataset Save) and shows a messages--warning block in the editor. An htmx:confirm and htmx:beforeRequest guard does the same for requests whose target contains the editor but which come from outside it: Add question and the move and delete buttons on other questions, which redraw the whole list. A beforeunload handler asks before leaving the page. The issue offered two options, saving open editors with the dataset or warning. The landed change takes the warning route. It landed in a larger Sprint 7 commit (8c8f8cd), documented in CHANGELOG.md and docs/user/usage/datasets.md.
